evidence.productionCapture: scripts/go_tui_capture.py with test/fixtures/go_tui_capture/agent_workspace.json against renderers built from the baseline and the candidate: all 15 grids (60x24, 80x24 and 140x40; workspace, row-base, row-delta, unknown-opcode and replacement) are identical.

snaps.from: 2 columns between modeline segments (file, position, message, search, extension, resync)
snaps.reason: anatomy.md Modeline segments: the gap between segments is md, one column in the TUI.
The showcmd echo is a modeline segment, so it takes the same md gap as every other segment.

snaps.from: 2 columns between the picker title and its query
snaps.reason: anatomy.md Prompt and minibuffer covers the query row of a picker: prompt label to query is md, one column in the TUI. The groups after the query (marked count, loading, error) stay xl apart.

snaps.from: outer width whichKeyWidth()-2 with rows fitted to whichKeyWidth()-4, so the header pager and the footer's last hint wrapped onto two extra rows inside a frame that left only whichKeyWidth()-6 columns
snaps.to: whichKeyFrame() renders at whichKeyWidth() and gives rows its contentWidth (outer minus the border and whichKeyInsetH on each side)
snaps.reason: The budget and the padding now come from one frame. The panel is 2 columns wider and 2 rows shorter, and the pager and Esc close sit on their own rows' right edge. In a terminal of 24 columns or fewer the panel fills the width, so it now sits flush left (x = 0) instead of two columns in.
snaps.scenario: TestChromeTokenFrames which_key_80x24 (golden) and which_key_120x40; TestPopoversFitTheirRowsInsideTheirFrame which_key_20 and which_key_24

snaps.from: markdown rule of transcript inset + 1 + (width-4) dashes, ending 1 column before the edge
